cells.tense: You are standing at the edge of something shared and you can feel exactly what it still holds.
cells.ask: Name out loud, to one person in it, the thing you keep doing together — just the act, no verdict attached.
cells.core:
You know the difference between what in this shared thing still carries weight and what is only habit. That is not a small skill. Plenty of people inside a group cannot see the seams at all. You can, and you can say it without turning it into a verdict, which is why the seam stays visible instead of becoming a fight.

Here is what it costs. Seeing the edges means you are often a little ahead of the others in the room, and being ahead keeps you a half step out of it. The connection you are protecting is the thing your clear eye keeps you slightly apart from. So you carry the reading and stand outside the reading, both at once.

Say the thing out loud and let them hold it with you. Then you are inside it again. That is the balance: you keep the eye and stop paying for it with distance. Nothing gets lost if what you see becomes shared.
cells.sheetLine: You can see what still carries weight. Say it out loud.
cells.place: where things get weighed and set back level

cells.tense: You are braced for this shared thing to end before it has given you any reason to be.
cells.ask: Stay through one more ordinary gathering and change nothing about how you hold yourself in it.
cells.core:
You are walking out the door before the door is there. Something shared still has weight, and you are already living past it — rehearsing the goodbye, reading every quiet stretch as the first sign, deciding what you will keep when it is over. None of that has happened. You have moved your attention so far ahead that you are no longer actually in the room you are in.

The bracing looks like clarity. It is not clarity, it is armor, and it costs you the exact thing you are guarding against losing. People can feel a person who has one foot out. They stop bringing you the real thing, because you have already told them, without saying it, that you are leaving.

So do the smaller thing for a while. Show up once more, at full weight, and let the goodbye stay unwritten. If it really is ending, you will know from something in front of you and not from a story you wrote. Stay first. Read later.
cells.sheetLine: You're packing for a departure nobody has announced.
cells.place: where things get weighed and set back level

cells.tense: You crossed a threshold in something shared and you are still standing on the near side of it.
cells.ask: Put one honest sentence about where you stand with them in front of a person and let their answer land.
cells.core:
Something in a shared thing shifted, and you took the reading and kept it. You know what the group's story actually is now, what it costs to keep it going, what you would say to make it truer. None of that has reached anyone. It stays in you, and the longer it stays the heavier it gets.

What you are carrying is the sense of the whole thing, and that sense is real. It has just not been set down where anyone else can look at it with you. So you hold the shape of the relationship alone, and then wonder why you feel outside it.

The way back is not a big conversation. One sentence, said plainly, to one person. You do not have to have solved the thing first. You can stop being the only one who owns it. Their answer will tell you something the version in your head cannot. Say the sentence, then listen past your own editing.
cells.sheetLine: You crossed over a while back. You're still calling it later.
cells.place: where things get weighed and set back level

cells.tense: You are already adjusting what is fair in this shared thing, and you are describing it as just how it goes.
cells.ask: Write down one thing you have quietly corrected for the group this month and read it back to yourself.
cells.core:
You have been rebalancing this shared thing for a long time, mostly under the table. Softening a comment, taking the smaller share, giving someone the benefit of the doubt before they asked, letting a slight slide so the evening holds. That is steady work, and it holds the thing at a level other people get to stand on.

You do not count any of it. Ask and you will say the group found its own way, that it evens out, that this is just how you are. The hand on the scale is yours and you have filed it under habit.

The cost is quiet: you keep at it without registering it, so you end up feeling spent without knowing why, and nobody knows to thank you because nobody knows it happened. Put one of those corrections down on paper where you can see it. Not to be paid back. Just to be yours. Once it is visible, you can decide when to stop doing it for free.
cells.sheetLine: You keep rebalancing the group and calling it nothing.
cells.place: where things get weighed and set back level
